senses.gloss: to discharge, vomit, give out. Y. B. Kam. I, 2ᵇ top [read:] היתה מהלכת ופוֹלֶטֶת על עשבים if the animal walked and discharged on plants.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 10:11">Ter. X, 11</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 110b">Ḥull. 110ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="B00898"><he>בָּלַע</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 3:6">Ber. III, 6</cite> <he>שפָּלְטָה שכבת וכ׳</he> who discharged the (conceived) semen virile.
<cite ref="Pesachim 118b:4">Pes. 118ᵇ</cite> <he>פְּלוֹט אותן ליבשה</he> throw their bodies out on the dry land; a. fr.

<cite ref="Niddah 61a:63">Nidd. 61ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>הפליט</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 14:13">Gen. XIV, 13</cite>) <he>זה עוג שפ׳ מדור וכ׳</he> that was Og who escaped the fate of the generation of the flood.
Num. R. s. 9 לא פָלְטוּ did not escape (punishment); a. fr.—V. פָּלֵט.—3) to save.
<cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 27:2">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXVII</cite> <he>ופְלָטוֹ הק״בה מידו</he> and the Lord saved him from his (Samael’s) power.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 19b:19">Snh. 19ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Q01007"><he>פלטיאל</he></cite>, <cite ref="II Samuel 3:15">II Sam. III, 15</cite>) <he>שפלטו אל מן וכ׳</he> for God saved him from sin; a. e.

<cite ref="Chullin 121a:8">Ḥull. 121ᵃ</cite> <he>בשר שפְּלָטַתּוּ סכין</he> flesh which the knife has taken off, i.e. which came off in flaying, v. <cite ref="M00625"><he>מוּרְדְּקָא</he></cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 121a:10">ib.</cite> <he>מקצתו פלטתו חיה</he> an animal tore one portion of the flesh off; <cite ref="Chullin 124a:20">ib. 124ᵃ</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be saved. Tanḥ. Sh’moth 17 ויִתְפַּלֵּט ממנו וכ׳ and Noah and his children shall be saved from it (the flood).
